title: Suppression of cytomegalovirus latency mechanisms through regulatory effects of specialized neutrophil granulocytes in recurrent sepsis
summary: Patients with recovering sepsis are susceptible to the occurrence of viral infections that they have already had in the past. One example of this is infection with cytomegalovirus (CMV). In this study, blood samples will be taken and analyzed in the laboratory to determine whether white blood cells are still able to respond appropriately to CMV contact during recovering sepsis.

interventions.name: Patients who initially improved after sepsis with a SOFA score greater than or equal to 2 but now show signs of a new infection with systemic inflammation in the blood (routine laboratory tests) will be included in the study after giving their informed consent. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Sepsis survived within the last month with SOFA score greater than or equal to 2.
- CMV seropositivity (detection of anti-CMV IgG)
- Increase in banded granulocytes to greater than or equal to 5% in routine laboratory tests
Exclusion criteria:
- Pre-existing drug-induced immunosuppression
- Malignant hematological condition
- Known infection with human immunodeficiency virus
